key_insight: The paper introduces native de Rham neural classes that guarantee outputs in H(div) or H(curl) for every parameter setting, while localizing discontinuities to explicit potential terms.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-informed surrogates for PDEs with discontinuous coefficients, interface jumps, curl-curl fields, transport shocks, and conservation laws without mesh-based finite element emulation.
method: Build neural fields as images of scalar/componentwise networks under fixed de Rham operators.
Use regular-decomposition forms where jumps are carried only by the potential term and the remaining field is H^1-smooth.
Train with a first-order system least-squares loss posed in the natural weak spaces, including H^-1 sources and H^1/2 boundary data.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents the method analytically and by PDE-class coverage, emphasizing exact space conformity and equivalence of the least-squares functional to the error rather than reporting numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Practical performance depends on how well interface geometry, coefficient discontinuities, and potential factors are specified or learned, which may be nontrivial for complex domains.
paper_title: FOSLS-deRhaNN: native de Rham neural classes for H(div) and H(curl) with applications to first-order system least-squares neural network methods for partial differential equations
